newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria leaves dual exchange rate untouched.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria leaves dual exchange rate untouched.

text.p: Nigeria's military government left its much-criticised policy of dual exchange rates unchanged in the 1997 budget announced on Saturday and said it was committed to a strong and stable naira.
"In respect of the exchange rate regime government would maintain the current system with the ultimate aim of a subsequent merger," General Sani Abacha said in his budget address.

International lending institutions and business have criticised the system under which the government has access to foreign exchange at a preferential rate of 22 naira per U.S. dollar against 80 naira per dollar offered at central bank auctions.
Abacha's tight control over money supply in 1995 and 1996 has led to a stabilisation of the naira and even a slight strengthening in value from 85 per dollar on the outside market in 1996.

"Monetary policy in 1997 is designed to complement fiscal policy in maintaining macro-economic stability, strengthening the external sector and the naira exchange rate, and stimulating economic growth and development," said Abacha.
He said foreign companies operating oil production joint ventures in Nigeria would have to continue to bring foreign exchange into the country through the central bank.
